subsystems.name: Graphene electrodes
subsystems.role: store charge by forming an electric double layer with ions from the electrolyte.

subsystems.name: Electrolyte
subsystems.role: supplies ions and sets the cell voltage window.
parts: organic solvent with salt (e.g. acetonitrile + tetraethylammonium tetrafluoroborate)
or ionic liquid for higher voltage

subsystems.name: Separator
subsystems.role: keeps the two electrodes apart while letting ions pass.
parts: porous polymer membrane (e.g. polypropylene or PTFE)

subsystems.name: Cell packaging
subsystems.role: contains the electrolyte and protects the electrode stack.

subsystems.name: Module electronics
subsystems.role: balances cells and manages temperature and safety.

buildSteps.title: Make graphene
buildSteps.detail: Graphene is produced by liquid-phase exfoliation of graphite, reduction of graphene oxide, or chemical vapour deposition; the route sets cost and quality.

buildSteps.title: Form electrode slurry
buildSteps.detail: Graphene is mixed with a conductive additive and binder in a solvent to make a coatable slurry.

buildSteps.title: Coat and dry
buildSteps.detail: The slurry is coated onto metal foil and dried to remove solvent.

buildSteps.title: Calender
buildSteps.detail: The coated foil is pressed between rollers to increase density and improve electrical contact.

buildSteps.title: Assemble cell
buildSteps.detail: Two electrodes are separated by a porous membrane and wound or stacked into a cell.

buildSteps.title: Fill electrolyte
buildSteps.detail: The cell is filled with electrolyte under vacuum and sealed.

buildSteps.title: Test and balance
buildSteps.detail: Cells are tested for capacitance and resistance, then assembled into modules with balancing electronics.

prerequisites.why: high-quality graphene is still costly; cheaper forms have lower conductivity.
supercapacitor electrodes need enormous surface area for ions to stick to.

prerequisites.tech: Stable electrolytes with wide voltage window
prerequisites.why: ionic liquids allow higher voltage but are expensive and viscous.
needed to optimise pore size for ion access.

pathway.milestone: commercial supercapacitors using graphene-enhanced electrodes in niche high-power roles
pathway.unlocks: faster charging and longer cycle life than batteries in regenerative braking, UPS and grid power smoothing.

pathway.milestone: energy densities above 20 Wh/kg with ionic-liquid electrolytes
pathway.unlocks: supercapacitors that can replace batteries in some short-duration applications.

pathway.milestone: hybrid devices combining battery-type and capacitor-type electrodes
pathway.unlocks: higher energy without losing fast charging.

pathway.milestone: flexible, solid-state graphene supercapacitors for wearables
pathway.unlocks: safe, thin power sources that charge in seconds.
